1.

By means of the instant petition, the petitioner has prayed for a writ of mandamus directing the respondents to pay compensation of Rs.28,22,050/- to him in pursuance of an award given by respondent no.4 under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956.

The case of the petitioner is that his double storied house built over Gata No.770 is subject matter of the acquisition proceedings and the award but the amount determined as compensation is not being released in his favour despite repeated applications.

He also places reliance on a joint inspection report dated 2.12.2022, according to which, double storied house, which is subject of matter of acquisition Rajeev Kumar Gupta vs National Highway Authority Of India And ... on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111274137/
1 proceedings, belongs to him.
2.

sentences.text: Ms. Akanksha Gaur, counsel for respondent no.2, on basis of instructions, states that one Uma Gupta S/o Late Raj Kumar Gupta has filed an application before respondent no.4 that a civil suit bearing no.48 of 2003 is pending before the civil court and until the suit is decided, compensation amount should not be released in favour of the petitioner.
He has also alleged that the petitioner is trying to withdraw the compensation amount on basis of fictitious documents.

3. Under Section 3-H (3) where several persons claim to be interested in the amount deposited as compensation in terms of the award, the Competent Authority is invested with the power to determine the persons who in its opinion are entitled to receive the amount payable to each of them.

Sub-section (4) stipulates that if any dispute arises as to the apportionment of the amount or any part thereof or to any person to whom the same or any part thereof is payable, the Competent Authority shall refer the dispute to the decision of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction within the limits of whose jurisdiction the land is situated.
4.
It appears that the claim of the petitioner to withdraw compensation amount is being resisted by Uma Gupta.
Consequently, the Competent Authority has to proceed in one of the manner noted above.

5. Accordingly, the instant petition is disposed of with direction to respondent no.4 to hear both the parties and pass speaking order having regard to the powers conferred upon him under the aforesaid provisions.
The order shall be passed by respondent no.4 within a period of twelve weeks from the date of communication of the instant order.
(Donadi Ramesh, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.) Order Date :- 15.9.2023
